correctness.rationale: The finite digit-carry NFA is derived exactly from a+db=n and the no-adjacent-one condition; carry c remains between 0 and d, so every digit path is enumerated. For any canonical positive n, both nonnegative addends have at most the length of n, and final carry zero is necessary and sufficient. The candidate exceptional DFA predicates are explicitly defined for each multiplier and match the stated binary words. The exhaustive BFS product-state counts are 4,6,18,9,41,29 and every outgoing final-one edge is tested for opposite acceptance; n=0 is checked separately. The included source and complete transition table permit exact replay; separate direct enumeration through 10000 agrees but is not the universal proof. The geometric-to-counting-function conversion follows from the exact inequality 4^k <= 3X+7.

originality.rationale: The claims were compared to the original fibbinary sequence A003714, the published fibbinary/Wythoff correspondence (arXiv:2405.18128), the explicit complement of the fibbinary set (arXiv:2406.12455), and a full-text source on sumsets of substitution fixed points (arXiv:2105.04959). Their objects or conclusions do not contain the exact family F+dF for d<=6, especially the coefficient-six excluded progression (4^k-7)/3. Actual external scientific searches for fibbinary sumsets, A003714 with coefficient six, and the candidate exception values did not identify an equivalent arithmetic theorem. Nearby recorded results for Moser-de Bruijn and other automatic sets concern different sets and are not implications. The mathematical mechanism and exceptional language have been directly compared rather than relying on different titles. This is originality within inspected evidence, not proof of universal publication priority.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed calculation might already contain the exact coefficient-six excluded family.
General automata tools could yield the equality without explicitly publishing its six-dilation numerical specialization; a fully exhaustive priority audit has not been performed.
This scientific review is not independent external validation.

value.rationale: The Fibonacci/Zeckendorf-linked fibbinary integers are a natural digit-restricted zero-density set. Classifying their sums with a small dilated second copy is a substantive additive basis question. The first six dilations reveal four sharply distinct regimes and especially the first nonperiodic sparse infinite exception family at coefficient six, with an exact counting law. This structural characterization is neither a routine finite numerical lookup nor a generic mere statement of decidability; it offers a motivated new arithmetic boundary and an explicit infinite description. No result is claimed for larger coefficients.
